rows: Human flourishing as excellent rational activity
Not a feeling-state or simple pleasure metric.
Human function as rational activity; virtue as excellence
Depends on whether a human function can do normative work.
Virtue between excess and deficiency relative to person and context
The mean is not arithmetic moderation or political centrism.
Stable disposition to act and feel appropriately
Virtue includes affective training, not just rule compliance.
This is the action-guidance engine, but it resists algorithmic rules.
Practice must be socially shaped; repetition alone can train vice.
Health and wealth as preferred/dispreferred, not truly good/bad
Stoicism targets false value judgments, not all emotion.
Internal goods and virtues required by social practices
Good as what a life-form needs for flourishing
Natural-kind reasoning is powerful but contested for humans.
